10 Signs Your Website Needs a Redesign (And What to Do About It)

Is your website helping or hurting your business? Here are 10 warning signs that your site is due for an overhaul — plus a roadmap to fix it.

Your website is your 24/7 salesperson. If it is not working while you sleep, it is working against you. Here are the 10 signs that tell you it is time for a redesign.

1. Your Site Takes More Than 3 Seconds to Load

Google research is clear: 53% of mobile visitors abandon a page that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. If your site is slow, you are losing half your potential customers before they even see your offer. Test your speed with Google PageSpeed Insights.

2. It Is Not Mobile-Friendly

Over 60% of web traffic is mobile. If your site requires pinch-to-zoom, has buttons too small to tap, or breaks on phones, you are telling the majority of your visitors to leave. Mobile-first is not a trend — it is the default.

3. You Are Not Getting Leads

A beautiful website with zero leads is an expensive decoration. If your contact forms sit empty and your phone does not ring, your site has a conversion problem. This is usually due to weak CTAs, confusing navigation, or no clear value proposition.

4. Your Competitors Outrank You

Search "your service + your city." If you are not on page one, your website is invisible to 95% of searchers. Poor SEO architecture, slow speed, thin content, and missing structured data all hurt rankings.

5. The Design Looks Dated

Web design trends evolve. A site that looked modern in 2019 looks ancient today. Dated design signals to visitors that your business might be dated too. First impressions form in 50 milliseconds — and they are hard to undo.

6. Your Bounce Rate Is Above 70%

Bounce rate measures visitors who leave without interacting. A high bounce rate means your site is not delivering what visitors expect. Common causes: slow load times, misleading headlines, poor design, or unclear value propositions.

7. You Cannot Update Content Yourself

If every blog post, photo change, or text edit requires a developer, your website is a bottleneck. Modern sites use CMS platforms that let non-technical users manage content easily.

8. It Does Not Reflect Your Current Business

Businesses evolve. Services change. Team members come and go. If your website still shows offerings you retired two years ago, it is actively confusing potential customers.

9. No Analytics or Tracking

If you cannot answer "how many visitors did we get last month?" or "what is our most popular page?" you are flying blind. Data-driven decisions require data. A modern website has analytics baked in from day one.

10. You Are Embarrassed to Share Your URL

This is the most honest sign of all. If you hesitate to send someone to your website, it is not doing its job. Your website should be your best salesperson — not a source of shame.

What to Do Next

If 3 or more of these apply to you, it is time to act. Here is the priority order:

  1. Audit your current site. Use free tools like PageSpeed Insights, GTmetrix, and Google Search Console.
  2. Define your goals. What should your website accomplish? Leads? Sales? Awareness?
  3. Set a budget. Be realistic about what a quality site costs. (See our pricing breakdown.)
  4. Find the right partner. Look for someone who asks about your goals, not just your colors.
  5. Plan the content. Great design with weak copy is still a weak site.
